Lofty uses FastAPI to serve endpoints, handle chat requests, manage voice and memory APIs, and deliver frontend static files.
Lofty stores session messages and user preferences in a JSON-backed memory file, with helper classes for saving, loading, and retrieving session state and preferences.
Lofty integrates with Ollama for local model inference, calling the Ollama API endpoint to generate responses and support model selection via environment variables.
LangGraph is used for orchestrating tool-aware assistant behavior, defining state graphs, routing between model responses and tool execution, and supporting multi-step workflow execution.
Lofty can call tools such as open_url, open_app, list_files, read_file, write_file, remember_preference, recall_preference, show_memory, and shell_command in a workspace-safe way.
Lofty uses a terminal-inspired browser UI with cinematic styling, card-based layout, theme support, voice controls, and a minimal command-driven presentation.
Lofty supports optional speech-to-text with faster-whisper and optional text-to-speech with pyttsx3, enabling voice input and spoken replies when configured.
Lofty enforces workspace-safe file paths, confirms risky actions, restricts tool actions to approved workspace directories, and uses safe path sanitization helpers.

lofty_backend.py is a Python backend module that implements the primary FastAPI assistant server, memory store, Ollama chat integration, shortcut commands, tool detection, and optional voice and TTS handling.

lofty_backend_enhanced.py is an enhanced version of the FastAPI backend that includes browser auto-open support, richer LangGraph/LangChain tool orchestration, shell command tools, and more advanced assistant state handling.

PREBUILT.py defines a Lovify-like assistant with LangGraph state graph setup, tool definitions, local app launching, URL opening, file access, memory management, and optional voice and model support for local assistant workflows.
assistant_workspace is a project folder used to store assistant-specific resources such as local models, memory files, and any files read or written by the assistant tools during execution.
The project README is stored in README.md and documents Lofty Terminal’s purpose, features, architecture, technology stack, workflow, and key components.
Lofty parses prefix commands like lofty:link, lofty:search, and lofty:remember, routes them to specialized tool logic, and returns structured tool output when needed.
The memory store class loads session and preference data from the JSON file, saves updates, appends messages to sessions, and provides methods to access stored preferences and conversation history.
The main purpose is to create a privacy-friendly, local-first AI assistant prototype that is developer-friendly, tool-aware, voice-capable, and ready for portfolio or product-style demonstration.
Lofty offers conversational chat, local tool execution, workspace file operations, app launching, browser link opening, memory persistence, voice interaction, and a polished terminal-style UI.
Lofty uses Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, LangChain, LangGraph, Ollama, Pydantic, requests, faster-whisper, pyttsx3, sounddevice, numpy, scipy, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Lofty uses FastAPI to serve endpoints, handle chat requests, manage voice and memory APIs, and deliver frontend static files.
Lofty stores session messages and user preferences in a JSON-backed memory file, with helper classes for saving, loading, and retrieving session state and preferences.
Lofty integrates with Ollama for local model inference, calling the Ollama API endpoint to generate responses and support model selection via environment variables.
LangGraph is used for orchestrating tool-aware assistant behavior, defining state graphs, routing between model responses and tool execution, and supporting multi-step workflow execution.
Lofty can call tools such as open_url, open_app, list_files, read_file, write_file, remember_preference, recall_preference, show_memory, and shell_command in a workspace-safe way.
Lofty uses a terminal-inspired browser UI with cinematic styling, card-based layout, theme support, voice controls, and a minimal command-driven presentation.
Lofty supports optional speech-to-text with faster-whisper and optional text-to-speech with pyttsx3, enabling voice input and spoken replies when configured.
Lofty enforces workspace-safe file paths, confirms risky actions, restricts tool actions to approved workspace directories, and uses safe path sanitization helpers.

lofty_backend.py is a Python backend module that implements the primary FastAPI assistant server, memory store, Ollama chat integration, shortcut commands, tool detection, and optional voice and TTS handling.

lofty_backend_enhanced.py is an enhanced version of the FastAPI backend that includes browser auto-open support, richer LangGraph/LangChain tool orchestration, shell command tools, and more advanced assistant state handling.

PREBUILT.py defines a Lovify-like assistant with LangGraph state graph setup, tool definitions, local app launching, URL opening, file access, memory management, and optional voice and model support for local assistant workflows.
assistant_workspace is a project folder used to store assistant-specific resources such as local models, memory files, and any files read or written by the assistant tools during execution.
The project README is stored in README.md and documents Lofty Terminal’s purpose, features, architecture, technology stack, workflow, and key components.
Lofty parses prefix commands like lofty:link, lofty:search, and lofty:remember, routes them to specialized tool logic, and returns structured tool output when needed.
The memory store class loads session and preference data from the JSON file, saves updates, appends messages to sessions, and provides methods to access stored preferences and conversation history.
The main purpose is to create a privacy-friendly, local-first AI assistant prototype that is developer-friendly, tool-aware, voice-capable, and ready for portfolio or product-style demonstration.
Lofty offers conversational chat, local tool execution, workspace file operations, app launching, browser link opening, memory persistence, voice interaction, and a polished terminal-style UI.
Lofty uses Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, LangChain, LangGraph, Ollama, Pydantic, requests, faster-whisper, pyttsx3, sounddevice, numpy, scipy, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
